# Bardo Rogue — the gauntlet prompt

I want you to finish Bardo Rogue, a browser action-roguelike, at the level of Enter the Gungeon's
combat density and pixel-art dungeon craft and Hades' melee weight and run structure. It should be
utterly perfect: every hit lands with the full feedback chain, every enemy telegraphs, every frame
looks authored rather than assembled. It runs at a locked 60 fps in a normal browser. The theme is
the bardo, the space between death and rebirth.

Break it into the smallest pieces that can each be judged on their own and fan out sub-agents so
every piece gets its own builder. Pieces that touch shared state get one owner working in sequence;
never two agents on coupled work at the same time. The simulation in `src/sim/` is pure and
deterministic and must stay that way: no DOM, no pixi, no `Math.random`, no `Date`. Every gameplay
and feel number lives in `src/tuning.ts`. Keep `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm test` green; if you change
the sim, regenerate the pinned replay hashes with `pnpm record-bots` and never hand-edit one.

Every piece also gets a separate, fresh sub-agent as its critic. The critic looks only at the real
thing — rendered screenshots, tick-labelled motion strips for anything that moves, `__game.state()`
traces for behaviour, and headless metrics for balance — never at code and never at the builder's
notes. It compares ours blind, side by side, in both orders, against real screenshots of the bar. It
is a harsh critic whose default assumption is that it CAN tell which one is ours. "Good for a web
game" is a loss. "Good for AI" is a loss. It names the single biggest gap, points at the file and
frame where it shows, and sends the piece back.

Never copy the reference's art, names, characters, lore, or composition. Copying the bar's layout is
itself a gap under Originality, not progress.

/loop on every piece until its critic genuinely cannot tell which one the professionals shipped.
After each wave, one fresh agent inspects the whole game and smooths the seams: one art style, one
feel, no joins. Keep the progress page current so I can watch it from my phone. Don't stop until
every critic is utterly wowed, or until I stop the run.
rubric:
Score all seven axes 0-5 EVERY round so round 11 stays comparable to round 1. If no axis moves for two rounds the piece is stuck by arithmetic, not by feel.
1 Readability - one frame tells you what is happening and what will hurt you.
2 Material and light - surfaces have weight; light has a hierarchy and a focal point.
3 Feel chain - anticipation, contact, impact, recovery all present and proportionate.
4 Composition - a focal point, asymmetry with intent, nothing grid-snapped by accident.
5 Pixel integrity - grid-aligned, integer scale, no shimmer, one consistent sprite scale.
6 Density - how much is happening per second compared with the exhibits.
7 Originality - a fan of the stronger exhibit would not call ours a copy. Copying the other exhibit's composition is itself a gap here, never progress.

EVIDENCE LIMIT, state it in your verdict: the reference exhibits are stills. Timing therefore cannot be compared against them. Judge axis 3 against the acceptance criteria below using our own tick-labelled strip and trace, and say plainly that you did.
Feel-chain acceptance: is there an anticipation frame distinguishable from idle? Is there exactly ONE readable contact frame? Does the freeze last long enough to see and short enough not to stall? Does recovery overshoot and settle rather than snap? Does the visual peak land on the tick the trace says damage becomes possible?

Things critics in this domain miss without prompting:
- Sub-pixel effects. At 480x270 a 0.19px camera shake is not a subtle shake, it is NO shake. Compute it, do not eyeball it.
- Silence as a bug. If an input produces no visual and no sound, that is a defect, not restraint. Diff the action strip against the idle strip.
- Grading the still and ignoring the tick. "The arc lives 2 ticks past contact" is a gap; "feels floaty" is not.
- Pixel-scale mismatch. Soft full-resolution gradients over hard 16px pixels read as gloss over placeholder.
- Bilateral symmetry and grid-snapped placement. The room currently mirrors left to right down to the plant.
- Light at the frame edges while the centre, where the eye and the fight are, is the least lit area.
- Accepting a bot metric as evidence of fun. Bots are regression probes. They do not report delight, panic, or perceived fairness.

sword-swing.spec: The three-hit greatsword chain: anticipation, arc, contact, recovery, and a heavy third hit that reads as a commitment. Verified leads, do not spend a round rediscovering them: the heavy is only +4 startup ticks, +2 hit-stop, +60 degrees of arc and double damage — nothing in the world commits to it, so it reads as a big light hit rather than a greatsword. Movement is zeroed for 10 ticks during heavy startup (167 ms) and is barely perceived. The crescent arc with tapered trailing edge is already the best visual in the game; build on it, do not replace it. Consider hit-confirm recovery (connecting cancels earlier than missing), whiff commitment, aim steering during early startup only, and an authored lunge curve instead of the current uniform one. Responsive does not mean uncommitted: do not make all four phases equally cancellable.
sword-swing.protocol: Motion. Dev server must already be on :5173; never start a second. 1) `pnpm strip -- --scenario dummy --seed 1 --from the first attack press --frames 12 --every 2 --crop 176,88,128,96 --out <E>/strip.png` — tick-labelled, --stepwise discipline, NEAREST upscale only. 2) the sidecar `<E>/strip.png.json` state+event trace. 3) `pnpm poses -- --only swing --out <E>/poses.png`. 4) the single most load-bearing frame, 4x NEAREST crop, as `<E>/exhibit.png` — this is the blind-comparison exhibit and it must be the same medium as the reference. 5) startup/active/recovery tick counts read from the trace, written to `<E>/timing.json`. Same seed, same crop box, every round. DRIVE THE INPUT WITH DISCRETE PRESSES, never `--hold '{"attack":true}'`: the hold flag re-applies the input partial before every single step, which is mashing at 60 Hz and hides what a player's own timing produces. Attack is now a true edge (one press = one intention), so use the `--eval` hook to press once per swing at the earliest legal chain tick. A chain captured by per-tick re-pressing is a fiction.

hit-impact.spec: The moment a hit lands: freeze, flash, knockback, reaction, camera, sound. Verified leads: the camera is SILENT on light hits, which are ~90 percent of all swings. Shake is trauma squared times shakeMax, so traumaLight 0.22 yields 0.22^2 x 4px = 0.19 internal pixels — invisible at 480x270 — and the directional kick is gated on `ev.heavy || ev.killed` (presenter.ts:80) so light hits get none at all. Separately, TWO reward channels are dead code: `dodged` (a successful i-frame dodge-through, the most skill-expressive input in the game) and `enemyStagger` are both emitted by the sim and consumed ONLY by metrics — grep confirms zero presenter and zero audio consumers. The game says nothing when the player does the hardest thing in it. The kill shatter, blood decals that outlive the fight, and the poise rule (only the heavy staggers a brute) already work; keep them.

dodge-roll.spec: The dodge as the other half of the combat language: launch, invulnerable traversal, landing. Verified leads: 18 ticks, 44 px, i-frames on ticks 2-12. The economics are broken — 44px/18t = 146.7 px/s against a 95 px/s run speed, so rolling is strictly better travel, and a never-attacking dodge-spam bot stalls wave 1 indefinitely (brutes landed 2 attacks in 120 seconds because they can never catch a rolling player). The i-frame window itself is honest and pinned by an exact test; the surrounding economics are the defect. Consider a cost (cooldown or stamina), earlier i-frame onset so a correct read is rewarded rather than punished, direction latched at the exact input edge, and a landing with readable recovery instead of one generic easing curve. Preserve attack buffering through the roll. A generic 360-degree sprite spin reads as a programmer's roll.

brute.spec: The brute's sentence is 'get out of the red, then hit me'. Chase, 20-tick windup with aim tracking that commits 6 ticks before release, committed lunge, 34-tick recovery, and stagger only from the heavy finisher. The timings already sit in a fair readability band — the defect is that readability is COLOUR MEMORY, not geometry. All three enemies share one red tint, the tell is tint plus squash on a 16px sprite, and there is no ground-projected geometry telling the player where the danger will be. Fix readability so it survives a sprite swap. NOTE: `src/tuning.ts` and `src/render/presenter.ts` belong to the feel lane this wave. If your fix needs either, stop and report rather than editing them. SHARED FILES, not yours: `src/render/views/shared.ts` (EntityView and the common helpers) and `src/render/views/enemies.ts` (the per-kind dispatcher) are owned by no lane this wave. If your fix needs either, stop and report rather than editing them — a second lane is very likely reading the same lines.

caster.spec: The caster's sentence is 'cross the line or cut the bolt'. Range management, 24-tick aim with a dotted line that hardens at 66 percent, one cuttable bolt, cooldown, strafe. Bolt-cutting is the single best idea in this combat — melee answering ranged — and it is under-rewarded: it deletes a projectile and creates no offensive payoff, and metrics say it happens 0-3 times per full run. The whole aim state is punishable, which is good. Verified bug in your file: caster.ts calls `world.fireProjectile(...)` and then emits `boltFired` UNCONDITIONALLY, so a saturated caster claims a shot and enters recovery with no projectile (a harness agent is fixing that specific line right now — rebase on it, do not duplicate it). NOTE: `src/tuning.ts` and `src/render/presenter.ts` belong to the feel lane this wave; stop and report if you need them. SHARED FILES, not yours: `src/render/views/shared.ts` (EntityView and the common helpers) and `src/render/views/enemies.ts` (the per-kind dispatcher) are owned by no lane this wave. If your fix needs either, stop and report rather than editing them — a second lane is very likely reading the same lines. One coupling to know about: `BoltView` and `drawAimLine` live in your file but `BoltView` renders EVERY projectile, not just caster bolts. Changing it changes what other enemies' projectiles look like. Keep bolt visuals caster-specific unless the change is genuinely universal, and say which you did.

combat-hud.spec: Hearts, wave counter, banners, place-name plate, control hint — everything on screen during a fight. What exists is already decent and crisp: all text is pixel webfont at resolution 1 inside the 480x270 target. Two verified defects to fix while you are here: banner timers run on wall-clock render time rather than sim time, so banners desync from sim state under slow-motion and stepwise capture (a death capture showed 'WAVE 1' still on screen); and there are no gamepad glyphs despite gamepad input being fully wired — the hint text says 'WASD / mouse / click / space' to a controller player. Judge the HUD as an inhabited combat frame, not an empty overlay.
combat-hud.protocol: Still. `pnpm shot -- --scenario wave3 --seed 1 --ticks 500 --bot kite --stepwise 1 --out <E>/still.png` (a busy frame, not an empty room), plus a 2x NEAREST crop of the HUD corners as `<E>/crop.png` with the SAME crop box every round, plus a room-clear frame and a death frame. Same seed and ticks each round.

death-card.spec: The death moment and its card. The staging already works — 30 ticks of 0.25 slow-motion, the player's own sprite shatters, a red vignette closes in — and several audits called it the most art-directed moment in the game. What is wrong is the words. The card says 'YOU DIED' and 'press R', which is developer UX wearing a game's clothes, and the loudest authored voice in the entire build is a stock fighter-game announcer shouting FLAWLESS VICTORY over an indigo death-realm. Read VISION.md: you are already dead, losing a run is being pulled back to the bardo, not a game over. This is the cheapest place in the whole project to put the fiction into the game instead of the filename, and there is a latent motif nobody wrote down — a room floating in a starfield void, doors and windows opening onto star-sky, THE THRESHOLD. Also add the run summary that is missing. `ART_DIRECTION.md` at the repo root is the aim; cite it.
death-card.protocol: Still plus short motion. `pnpm strip -- --scenario wave1 --seed 5 --from <the killing blow> --frames 10 --every 3 --out <E>/strip.png` for the death sequence, plus the settled card as `<E>/exhibit.png` at 2x NEAREST. Same seed and start tick every round.

audio-bed.spec: Give the room a floor of sound and give the mix somewhere to grow. Verified state: the Web Audio layer is competent Foley — round-robin variants with anti-repeat, pitch variance, a synthesized bandpass-noise swish layered under every sword whoosh, layered per-event mappings — but there is ONE master GainNode, `play()` exposes no loop flag so ambience literally cannot play today, `fight.ogg` ships in the manifest and is never played, the `duckUntil` field is written and never read, and `duck()` lowers the WHOLE mix including the impact it should be making room for. Ship: master/music/ambience/sfx bus split, a loop and crossfade helper, one drone ambience, one two-layer combat loop crossfaded on `aliveEnemies() > 0`, and delete the fighter announcer. Audio must stay presentation-only and must never touch sim state. Load the `audio-design` skill in this repo before you start.
audio-bed.protocol: No image can judge sound; say so and grade with lowered confidence. Evidence: (1) the event-to-sound map rendered as a table, (2) the bus graph with gain and ducking curves as NUMBERS, (3) a 10-second OfflineAudioContext render of a full wave-1 fight written to `<E>/mix.wav` plus its waveform and peak/RMS per bus as `<E>/levels.json` — a mix that clips is a loss, (4) the event timeline from a replay. Judge structure and levels, not taste.
